q: Before this paper, what were the dominant sequence transduction (e.g. translation) models built from?
a: complex recurrent (RNN) or convolutional (CNN) neural networks with an encoder and a decoder; the best also connect encoder and decoder with attention

q: What is the new architecture called, and what is it based on?
a: the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms

q: What does the new architecture remove entirely?
Besides better quality, what two practical advantages did the experiments show?
a: more parallelizable and significantly less time to train

q: What BLEU score did it reach on WMT 2014 English-to-German?
How did the English-to-German result compare with the previous best results?
a: better than the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU

q: What did it reach on WMT 2014 English-to-French?
a: a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU of 41.8

q: How long and on what hardware was the English-to-French model trained, and how does that cost compare with earlier best models?
a: 3.5 days on eight GPUs; a small fraction of the training cost of the best previous models

q: Does the model work on tasks other than translation? Which one, and with how much data?
a: yes, English constituency parsing, with both large and limited training data
